alt: One-pan Portuguese Chicken and Potato Bake

region.label: Europe
region.cuisine_label: Paprika-and-lemon chicken bakes in a Portuguese style

summary: Thinly sliced potatoes, onion and capsicum get a head start in a garlicky lemon dressing, then bone-in chicken thighs rubbed with paprika and oregano roast on top of them. The potatoes cook in the chicken's drippings, so one pan gives the whole meal and a thin broth for mopping with bread.

ingredients.item: Chicken thighs, bone in and skin on
ingredients.note: The source also lists drumsticks or Marylands (whole leg quarters) as suitable; see the safety notes on timing.
Sweet, plain or smoked; the source allows any of the three.
The source lists it simply as coriander within a dry spice mix; ground is this project's reading.

ingredients.item: Extra virgin olive oil, for the chicken
Waxy potatoes, skin on, sliced 5 mm thick
ingredients.note: The source prefers waxy potatoes; floury ones also work but break up more easily.

ingredients.item: Red capsicum, seeded and cut into 3.5 cm squares
Extra virgin olive oil, for the potatoes

method.instruction: Heat the oven to 200°C conventional, or 180°C fan-forced. Both figures are stated by the source; neither is a conversion made here. The source names no shelf; a middle shelf is this project's ordinary default, not a source instruction.

Put all the potato-bake ingredients — potatoes, onion, capsicum, garlic, the 2 teaspoons of oregano, salt, pepper, oil and lemon juice — into a large roasting pan and toss well, pulling apart any potato slices stuck together. The source gives no pan dimensions.
Bake the vegetables on their own for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix all the chicken seasoning ingredients in a bowl, add the thighs and turn them until coated all over. Wash your hands and anything the raw chicken touched before handling the hot pan.
Take the pan out, set the thighs on top of the potatoes and tuck any loose skin underneath, then bake for 40 minutes, until the skin is golden.

Check the thickest thigh at the centre, clear of the bone. The source cooks to an internal 76°C; Health Canada's threshold for poultry pieces is 74°C internal (Safe cooking temperatures), so the source's figure already clears it. Use the thermometer, not the 40 minutes, as the test.
If the chicken is done but the potatoes are still firm, cover the chicken loosely with foil and return the potatoes to the oven until tender. Serve with the pan juices and bread.

yield_note: Serves 5, as stated by the source. Source times: 15 minutes preparation and 1 hour 5 minutes cooking (25 minutes for the vegetables alone, then 40 minutes with the chicken). The source gives no resting time, and none is invented here. Leftovers: the source says 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

caveats: Poultry must be cooked all the way through. Health Canada gives 74°C internal for poultry pieces; the source aims for 76°C. Measure the thickest piece at its centre, not touching bone, and do not rely on juice colour.
Raw chicken contaminates whatever it touches. Coat it in a bowl you then wash, and wash hands, board and knife before touching the vegetables or the serving dish.

Changing the cut changes the timing. The source says Marylands take longer and can go into the oven with the potatoes from the start; it also lists drumsticks as suitable. Whatever the cut, the thermometer decides, not the clock.
Leftovers: chill promptly once the steam has died down, keep no longer than the source's 3 days in the fridge, and reheat until the centre reaches 74°C (Health Canada's figure for leftovers).
